Prevention: Use disease free planting material obtained from the
FOHCREC Kade or a certified nursery
Gather and bury or burn all fallen fruits and leaves as this will help reduce the disease inoculum
Prune to remove unproductive and diseased branches after harvest to reduce humidity and increase air circulation in the orchard to reduce the disease
Carry out a routine disease management programme in areas where the disease is present
Do not intercrop as this will increase humidity and favour infection
Encourage other citrus farmers in the locality to use a routine management programme to reduce the incidence of the disease
Monitoring: Symptoms on the leaves appear as small spots, light-brown or greyish in the dry season, becoming black during the rains.
The spots often have a dark-brown margin and a prominent yellow halo.
On fruits the spots can be 10mm in diameter, raised or flat often surrounded by a yellow halo.
Diseased fruits ripen prematurely and drop or dry and remain on the tree
In areas where the disease does not occur check seedlings in nursery for symptoms on the leaves
In the orchard monitor new flushes and fruit after petal fall for symptoms at weekly intervals
Start direct chemical control if symptoms on leaves or fruits are seen
In areas where the disease is present start direct control measures as soon as new leaves start to flush
Direct Control (Non-chemical): There are no green direct control methods for this disease
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
